\caption{Six saliency models and the local-null family on the Kanizsa displays. Effects are differences in $r$, the map mass inside the figure divided by the mass inside the figure plus on the inducers, between the illusory display and a control whose inducers are rotated by 180$^\circ$ or 90$^\circ$; means over 60 configurations, with 95\% cluster-bootstrap CIs in brackets for the 180$^\circ$ effect, the core effect and the slope (the CIs of the 90$^\circ$ effects and ratios of DeepGaze IIE and MSDB are given in the text). Core: the same contrast for figure pixels more than 30~px from the inducer discs. Ratios: the effect with every inducer rotated by 20$^\circ$ in the same direction (uniform) or in alternating directions, divided by the aligned effect; computed only where the aligned CI lies above 0 (n.e. otherwise). Slope: change of the aligned effect per unit support ratio (0.3 to 0.7). Local nulls: corner-detector, ink and edge-energy maps blurred with a Gaussian of $\sigma$~px; the edge null at $\sigma = 25$~px is the edge-energy null of the survey. n.c.: not computed for this model.}
